originalTitle: Raúl Jiménez’s injury-time penalty salvages point for Wolves against Blackburn
summary: Wolves drew 2-2 against Blackburn in the Championship season opener after Raúl Jiménez scored a spot-kick deep in stoppage time
content: Raúl Jiménez marked his return to Wolves with the stoppage-time equaliser that saved them from an embarrassing start to their return to the Championship. The Mexico striker, who scored against England during the World Cup, came off the bench to convert a penalty given for handball by Ryan Alebiosu that would have had VAR questioning whether the defender was in the area when Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross struck his arm. One minor consolation from Wolves’ relegation is that the video assistant referee is no longer their problem. Jiménez, who had bought scarves for all supporters in the South Bank in gratitude for their welcome home, tucked away his first goal in this second spell for the club he graced during their recent heyday before leaving for Fulham. “He’s an important striker,” César Peixoto, Wolves’ new head coach said. “He lives for scoring and making goals. Raúl is a key player for us. He helped the team inside and outside the pitch but we have to go slowly with him because he is 35 years old and comes back from the World Cup. We want him to stay good and scoring for us is good for him and for the team.” Goals from Sean McLoughlin and Andri Gudjohnsen allowed Blackburn to provide Wolves with a reality check after Marshall Munetsi had scored early. Confidence is a fragile commodity and, after their decision to replace Rob Edwards with a manager with no experience of English football, the Wolves board know that their supporters’ patience is thin. Leading Gil Vicente to sixth place in the Portuguese first division does not make Peixoto a guaranteed winner. Conceding the equaliser, through Jiménez’s first goal for Wolves in 1,311 days, denied unfancied Blackburn a deserved victory after Wolves lost their shape. Tony Mowbray, their head coach, felt the penalty decision was harsh. “I’ve just been shown an angle by my analyst where he [Alebiosu] is outside the box; another angle I’m told shows he’s just inside the box. I just felt like more and more decisions were starting to sway their way,” the former West Brom manager said. “It’s harsh to take because I don’t think they deserved that second goal.” Molineux was awash with fading golden sunlight and rising optimism at kick-off. A summer that started with such a surprising managerial departure was promising to end with renewed faith in the team’s direction of travel, until Peixoto’s admired high press came unstuck as his team started to “play with their hearts more than their heads”. The Blackburn defence had split generously to allow Munetsi a clean run through on to Fer López’s sumptuous pass. The left-footed finish from the Zimbabwean, himself coming back to Molineux after a loan at Paris FC, strengthened the feelgood factor. Peixoto’s tactics do currently lead to gaps on transition. Blackburn, who have not done so much in the transfer market to suggest they should aim higher than last season’s 20th place, got behind Wolves on several occasions. It was no great surprise when, from Ryoya Morishita’s superb right-wing cross, McLoughlin headed beyond Dan Bentley to equalise. Some of Wolves’ best business this summer has been bringing players back to Molineux. While Jiménez started the night on the bench, after a late start to pre-season following his impressive World Cup for Mexico, López was the classiest player on view. Back from a loan at Celta Vigo, he has been invited to make the No 10 position his own, and the Spaniard nearly regained Wolves the lead only to curl his shot wide. Blackburn continued to benefit from Wolves’ soft centre however. Oladapo Afolayan’s shot needed tipping over by Bentley before the right winger again got space down Wolves’ left – where David Møller Wolfe, in for the injured Hugo Bueno, showed he is still not match fit after his World Cup endeavours with Norway – to cross for Gudjohnsen to turn in Rovers’ second goal. “The team lost some organisation and played with their heart rather than their head and brains,” Peixoto said. “It’s a lesson for us in the future, we need to stay with mental stability for the 90 minutes.” By the hour mark, the South Bank were swirling their Jiménez scarves above their heads and chanting “Si Señor” in honour of the veteran striker who was such an esteemed figure at Molineux for five of the club’s best years in modern times. Before his horrific head injury, he was the pivotal attacking player as Nuno Espírito Santo’s team reached the later stages of the FA Cup and Europa League. The scene was set for the Mexican. Could he deliver? Si, señor.
chineseTitle: 劳尔·希门尼斯在伤停补时阶段的点球为狼队对阵布莱克本的比赛挽救了一分
chineseSummary: 劳尔·希门尼斯在伤停补时阶段攻入点球，狼队在英冠赛季揭幕战中2-2战平布莱克本
chineseContent: 劳尔·希门尼斯在补时阶段扳平比分，标志着他重返狼队，帮助狼队摆脱了重返英冠的尴尬开局。这位在世界杯期间对阵英格兰的比赛中进球的墨西哥前锋，替补出场，罚进了瑞安·阿莱比苏因手球而判罚的点球，当杰克逊·查楚亚的传中击中他的手臂时，VAR会质疑这名后卫是否在禁区内。狼队降级的一个小小的安慰是视频助理裁判不再是他们的问题。希门尼斯为南岸的所有球迷买了围巾，以感谢他们欢迎回家，在前往富勒姆之前，他在俱乐部最近的鼎盛时期为他打进了第二个进球。 “他是一名重要的前锋，”狼队新任主教练塞萨尔·佩肖托说道。 “他为得分和进球而生。劳尔是我们的关键球员。他在球场内外帮助了球队，但我们必须慢慢地对待他，因为他已经35岁了，刚刚从世界杯回来。我们希望他保持出色的状态，为我们进球对他和球队都有好处。”肖恩·麦克劳林和安德里·古德约翰森的进球让布莱克本在穆涅茨早早进球后为狼队提供了现实检验。信心是一种脆弱的商品，在决定用一位没有英格兰足球经验的主教练取代罗布·爱德华兹后，狼队董事会知道他们的支持者的耐心很薄弱。带领吉尔·维森特在葡萄牙甲级联赛中获得第六名并不意味着佩索托一定会成为冠军。希门尼斯为狼队攻入 1,311 天以来的首个进球，最终丢掉了扳平比分的进球，让不被看好的布莱克本在狼队失去状态后失去了应得的胜利。他们的主教练托尼·莫布雷（Tony Mowbray）感受到了处罚决定
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
